Second pass. The June 4, 2019 Riverside general municipal election, per the county candidate proof list dated April 24, 2019, had City Council Wards 1, 3, 5 and 7 only, with no mayoral contest. The county statement of vote for June 4, 2019 shows four City of Riverside council contests, for Wards 1, 3, 5 and 7, which match the proof list, and no mayoral contest. The May 7, 2019 county candidate list has no City of Riverside contest. The county calendar for November 5, 2019 describes a Uniform District Election Law election, which covers special districts and not city offices. A county statement of vote for November 5, 2019 was not found, so the absence of a Riverside mayoral contest on that date rests on the calendar type and not on a results document. The 2016 and 2020 mayoral elections are recorded in the results file, and the 2020 winner is shown by the city clerk as elected in 2020. No vacancy or special mayoral election appears in these documents.

The March 3, 2020 first round held a Riverside mayor contest. The November 3, 2020 county statement of votes cast shows a two-candidate runoff between Patricia Lock Dawson and Andrew S. Melendrez Jr. The runoff decided the office and is recorded in riverside_results.json.

Riverside City Charter Sec. 400(a) sets a four-year term for the Mayor. Sec. 500 says general municipal elections for Mayor are held on the primary election date set by the State in United States Presidential election years. Sec. 500 also names the June 8, 2021 election as a Councilmember election for Wards 2, 4 and 6 only. The 2020 mayoral winner took office after the November 2020 election, and the 2024 mayoral election is recorded in the results file. The city clerk page states the next mayoral election is on March 7, 2028. The charter provisions were amended on November 3, 2020 and apply to this year. No special mayoral election appears in the official sources inspected.
